article_html:
ISTANBUL: Turkiye has nominated Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, head of the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), to be the next UN secretary-general, a diplomatic source confirmed on Saturday.

The move came after a deadlock in the selection process, with the latest straw poll at the UN Security Council held on Friday returning an inconclusive outcome.

Contacted by AFP, the Turkish diplomatic source confirmed that the nomination letter dated Friday from Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan was submitted to the presidents of the UN General Assembly and the Security Council.

In the letter, published by Turkish media, Erdogan said the nomination reflected Ankara's commitment to "effective multilateralism" at a time when "geopolitical divisions are deepening and trust between nations is diminishing".

With more than four decades of experience in international relations and diplomacy, Sinirlioglu has held some of Turkiye's highest diplomatic positions, including foreign minister and permanent representative to the United Nations, Erdogan said in the letter.

The choice of next UN chief would be crucial in steering the international community towards "a more peaceful, just and sustainable future" amid mounting global challenges, he added.

The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31.

Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 available in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided.

Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.

headline: Noah Kahan reacts to surprising shout out on TV show
subheadline: Noah Kahan gets namedropped on TV in hilarious moment
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Noah Kahan got casually namedropped on Love Is Blind while his fans are celebrating their excitement for his upcoming Last of the Bugs tour.

The Northern Attitude hitmaker took to Instagram and shared a video of himself watching the show when someone mentions, “I like grungy white men with beards. Put a baseball cap on," to which someone says, "Like a Noah Kahan type?”

In a hilarious turn of events, the first speaker said, “I don’t know who Noah Kahan is,” to which Kahan responded by writing, "Caught me off guard."

Fans flocked to social media and reacted to the now-viral moment, writing, "his reaction was the same as mine i was like don't talk about my mans like that," and "Why’s he looking at us like we said it."

A third chimed in, "aww he looks so cute here," and "CRYING HE HAD NO IDEA THEY WERE GOINF[sic] TO PLAY IN HIS FACE," wrote another.

While more added, "his little chuckle when she says 'idk who noah kahan is' LMAO" and "Lmaoo he's hilarious," as well as "i'm screaming."

headline: Why did US stock market crash? $2 trillion AI selloff, explained simply
subheadline: Nasdaq wipes out $2 trillion in October as AI spending fears deepen
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Wall Street closed October with a brutal selloff, erasing roughly $2 trillion from the Nasdaq-100’s market value as investors questioned whether the AI boom can justify its enormous costs.

The wipeout is slightly larger than SpaceX’s entire market value, with the index down more than 5.8% for the month.

The immediate trigger was disappointing corporate earnings.

Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage drop on record, losing more than $500 billion in market value, after reporting $9.1 billion in negative free cash flow driven by AI infrastructure spending and missing expectations in its core search advertising business.

Amazon disclosed negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the past 12 months and expects capital expenditure of approximately $220 billion this year.

Intel collapsed nearly 29% in a single day after an explosion at its Israeli manufacturing facility disrupted production, and an estimated $600 million revenue hit over two quarters, compounded by weakening PC demand.

Reddit fell more than 36% for the week after warning that Google’s AI-generated search answers were reducing traffic to its platform. Enterprise software stocks also suffered, with ServiceNow down about 34% and Fortinet losing 24%.

This selloff is being fueled by concerns regarding the level of investment being made in the AI sector.

According to JPMorgan, capital expenditures on artificial intelligence across the globe will hit $900 billion by 2026, while Morgan Stanley predicts it will top a trillion dollars next year.

The rising cost of credit is making debt-financed investment harder to justify; for instance, Microsoft is planning to issue a $25 billion bond, its first investment-grade offering in the US in more than nine years.

However, not all was bad news. Microsoft reported high demand for its cloud products, Google saw its cloud revenues more than double, and Meta beat market expectations when it comes to revenue growth.

AMD and Nvidia’s earnings are awaited now.

The unexpected news has also left the band with no choice but to cancel two concerts in Germany.

The band shared an update online, saying that Gillan was currently in hospital and would not be able to perform. The group, however, was supposed to play in Leipzig on October 31 before heading to Hamburg for another show on November 1.

Both concerts got to be called off because of the singer's health situation.

READ MORE: Macklemore makes major statement after Ed Sheeran stage moment

In its statement, Deep Purple said, “This comes as a result of a medical emergency involving Ian Gillan, which has resulted in his current hospitalization.”

The band, meanwhile, has not explained what happened to the singer but it has promised fans that the shows will be arranged again. It, moreover, also confirmed that people who already bought tickets will be able to use them for the new dates.

Soon after the announcement, fans began sharing messages for Gillan, with many hoping he would feel better soon.

headline: Jackie Chan makes comeback with 'The Shadow's Edge II'
subheadline: 'The Shadow’s Edge II' is expected to bring more action
author: Hina Ali
article_text:
Jackie Chan is set to return in another action film as The Shadow’s Edge II has officially started production.

The actor will once again play his role in the sequel, which comes after the first movie brought him back into the spotlight for his action scenes.

The first film showed Chan in a serious police role as he faced a group of dangerous criminals. It was a different kind of story for the actor but it gave him plenty of chances to show the action skills that made him famous.

READ MORE: Jackie Chan death hoax spreads online as fake ‘1954-2026' posts go viral; actor is alive

His fight scenes, however, also reminded viewers why he became such a big name in action movies.

Now, the story is not over yet. The second film will bring back the same team that worked on the first one, giving the story another chapter.

This time, the trouble is expected to be bigger, with more criminals and new dangers for Chan's character to face.

The first movie also featured Tony Leung Ka fai, who played an important part in the story. Moreover, the makers have not yet shared full details about the new film or its cast.

READ MORE: Rock legend Ian Gillan rushed to hospital as band cancels shows

With filming now underway, Chan is getting ready for another big fight on screen. The sequel is expected to bring more action and give viewers another look at the actor in a role that has already won attention.

headline: Canelo Alvarez vs Christian Mbilli: Time, where to watch, ringwalk schedule
subheadline: Canelo Alvarez challenges Christian Mbilli for WBC title in Riyadh
author: Web Desk
article_text:
On Saturday night in Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Saul "Canelo" Alvarez looks to return to the winner's circle and capture super middleweight gold by taking on unbeaten WBC champion Christian Mbilli.

The pay-per-view fight on DAZN will be Alvarez's first in the ring since suffering a unanimous decision defeat to Terence Crawford last September in 2025. The 36-year-old Mexican (63-3-2, 39 KOs) takes to the ring as the challenger for the first time since his 2022 weight class promotion, where he fought Dmitry Bivol. Alvarez enters the bout with a record of 28 total fights against title contenders, including a mark of 25-3 in those championship bouts. Coverage starts at 1 p.m. ET, with ring walks scheduled for 4:30 p.m. ET.

Mbilli (29-0-1, 24 KOs) at age 31 comes into the contest with almost two inches of reach advantage and an aggressive pressure fighting style. The Cameroonian-born Frenchman was promoted to world champion in January and drew Lester Martinez in a split decision on the Canelo-Crawford undercard.

Boxing analyst Raul Marquez believes the bout may work out well for Alvarez stylistically. "Alvarez, you know, he's got great technique to deal with opponents who come forward because he knows how to box them very well. And he's an excellent counter-puncher and excellent body puncher," Marquez stated. He tipped Alvarez by a unanimous decision but noted: "However, if Canelo fights like that against Mbilli" — as he did in his fight against Crawford — "it's going to be a very long night for him."

The Hall of Fame broadcaster Al Bernstein is not as sure about it, tipping Mbilli reluctantly. "When you look at the fight from a boxing perspective and say, 'OK, who is more likely to win this fight,' I think Mbilli," he stated, mentioning Alvarez's age and the level of his decline.

Alvarez is a big favourite at -330, while Mbilli is priced at +250. The total rounds line is set at 10.5.

headline: India opposition parties hold mock impeachment of poll chief
subheadline: Opposition parties accuse election commission of favouring Modi's BJP through nationwide voter-roll revision
author: AFP
article_text:
India's political opposition staged a symbolic impeachment of the election commissioner on Saturday to protest against a revision of voter lists that they say could unfairly benefit the ruling party.

The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world's largest democracy over the last month.

The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Both the Election Commission and the BJP deny the allegations.

On Saturday, opposition parties gathered at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in the capital New Delhi, re-enacting a parliamentary session.

They held mock impeachment proceedings, which have no constitutional or legal force, against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"The motion we have brought forward today is aimed at safeguarding the dignity of a constitutional institution," Kharge said.

"Our intention is for the Election Commission to function impartially, in line with the spirit of the constitution."

Under the constitution, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a parliamentary process requiring a special majority.

Senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the opposition had resorted to the symbolic exercise as they "have nowhere else to go".

"We have no other option. Every single institution... is closed for us," Gandhi said.

The event came a day before a major opposition rally in Delhi backed by the Cockroach Janta Party, an online youth-led movement that also supports the campaign against the voter-roll revision.

Home Minister Amit Shah said the BJP was ready to hold a special session of parliament to discuss the revision.

"But they (the opposition) have no intention of speaking there. They refuse to let the parliament function. Instead, they just create a ruckus," he said.

India's political opposition staged a symbolic impeachment of the election commissioner on Saturday to protest against a revision of voter lists that they say could unfairly benefit the ruling party.

The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world's largest democracy over the last month.

The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Both the Election Commission and the BJP deny the allegations.

On Saturday, opposition parties gathered at the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in the capital New Delhi, re-enacting a parliamentary session.

They held mock impeachment proceedings, which have no constitutional or legal force, against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"The motion we have brought forward today is aimed at safeguarding the dignity of a constitutional institution," Kharge said.

"Our intention is for the Election Commission to function impartially, in line with the spirit of the constitution."

Under the constitution, the chief election commissioner can only be removed through a parliamentary process requiring a special majority.

Senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the opposition had resorted to the symbolic exercise as they "have nowhere else to go".

"We have no other option. Every single institution... is closed for us," Gandhi said.

The event came a day before a major opposition rally in Delhi backed by the Cockroach Janta Party, an online youth-led movement that also supports the campaign against the voter-roll revision.

Home Minister Amit Shah said the BJP was ready to hold a special session of parliament to discuss the revision.

"But they (the opposition) have no intention of speaking there. They refuse to let the parliament function. Instead, they just create a ruckus," he said.

headline: Binance says it has covered 90% of losses from $6.3bn hack so far
subheadline: Binance pledges to cover remaining losses; users will not bear the impact
author: Reuters
article_text:
Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday it has been able to replace 90% of the amount stolen after a record $6.3 billion hack of its platform, by using company money to buy new tokens.

The remaining 10% consists of tokens that are less liquid, which means they may take longer to buy, it said in a statement posted on X.

"We've now replenished 90% of the stolen assets, and we're committed to covering the remaining 10%. Our users will not bear the financial impact of this incident," co-CEO Richard Teng said on X on Saturday.

Crypto prices fell on Friday, while Binance — the world's biggest crypto exchange — sought to reassure customers that their funds were safe after losing more than $6 billion worth of crypto in a hack which analysts blamed on North Korea.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a "complex attack" involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate.

After the hack, the exchange stopped allowing customers to withdraw their funds, but it said on Saturday it was still on track to re-open withdrawals on Sunday.

Binance said it has set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses.

The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures insurance fund, and the company's own corporate treasury, it said on X.

Binance also said it had taken a new snapshot of assets held on its platform as of 0000 GMT on October 31, as part of its proof-of-reserves process.

Users holding the 10 listed tokens — BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC — would be able to verify that their assets were backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio once the full proof was available, it said.

headline: Olivia Rodrigo takes over internet with hilarious response to fan's costume

Olivia Rodrigo won fans' respect even more this Halloween as she was able to laugh at herself when a fan parodied one of her photoshoots.

The drivers license hitmaker went viral for the photoshoot at the time as well, and it caught much traction since the makeup, lighting, and clothing, all ended up working against her favour.

headline: What is Reddit's logged-in model? Everything to know about platform's major shift
subheadline: Reddit to become primarily logged-in as AI search erodes traffic
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Reddit has announced it will shift to a primarily logged-in experience, marking one of the most significant changes in its 21-year history as AI-powered search drains traffic from the open web.

This means Reddit wants most people to use the platform while signed in to a Reddit account instead of browsing anonymously as a visitor who arrives via a Google search or a shared link.

Under the shift, logged-out users would see a restricted version of Reddit, likely just the homepage and the specific content they clicked on, while features like voting, commenting, subscribing, and personalised feeds would require an account.

As per the company, there are three primary reasons driving this move, i.e., protecting its data from AI scraping, better ad targeting, and higher engagement.

Reddit's content will provide valuable training data for the AI models. Having a logged-in wall will make mass scraping much more difficult and strengthen Reddit's negotiating position when dealing with the licensing of its content to AI companies.

Signals of logged-in users will allow Reddit to personalise advertisements and make money from that. As Huffman explained, over 80% of Reddit's monetisation is done through the app and logged-in users.

The search traffic is plummeting. Reddit reported referrals were down by over 1 million per week on average in October, mainly due to Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode that answer questions without redirecting users to websites. Daily active US users are down by 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, and Reddit predicts "a low double-digit percentage" decrease next quarter.

Reddit plans to try out the logged-in experience in Q4 in certain countries outside of the US market, but no information was provided regarding any timeframe on a global scale.

headline: Maya Jama faces major career move as BBC reportedly makes big offer
subheadline: Maya Jama is busy filming the third series of Netflix's 'The Gentlemen'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Maya Jama have missed winning Celebrity Traitors but her time on the show can open another big door for her.

The presenter has reportedly caught the attention of BBC bosses, who are now hoping to bring her back to the channel.

Maya is already one of the familiar faces on ITV, where she presents Love Island. However, her recent appearance on Celebrity Traitors seems to have made BBC bosses think about giving her an even bigger role on television.

READ MORE: Maya Jama's bizarre 'Celebrity Traitors' outfit sparks hilarious reaction

During the show, Maya played a Traitor and managed to keep her secret hidden for most of the series. She surprised viewers with her clever moves and did not hold back when it came to taking out other players.

A source told The Sun that BBC bosses were impressed by how she connected with the show's huge audience. They reportedly believe she has the confidence, humour and personality to present some of their biggest shows.

Brining Maya back, moreover, was not easy maybe, as ITV is also keen to keep her.

READ MORE: Rock legend Ian Gillan rushed to hospital as band cancels shows

Maya first started her career at the BBC as a radio presenter before moving into television. She later became the host of Love Island in 2023.

She is also busy filming the third series of Netflix's The Gentlemen.

headline: Who are three women accusing Josh Jacobs? What police records reveal
subheadline: NFL to review new abuse allegations against Packers’ Josh Jacobs
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Three more women reported to law enforcement investigating Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs following his arrest in May, with accounts of alleged offences going back to 2021, according to documents obtained Friday from the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department.

The first woman: January 2022

The woman stated that she had been communicating with Jacobs for about six months and spent approximately 11 hours at his house before he became angry at her when she told him she did not have se* on her mind.

The alleged victim said that he took her phone and threw it in the swimming pool when she tried to leave, and pulled her hair, pushed her on the bed and threw her on the floor, stating, "I should kill you right now." She also claimed that he spit on her and choked her.

She said that she did not report it at the time because she was still friends with him and feared that no one would believe her.

The second woman: April 2021

She told police she had se* with Jacobs, and when the con**m broke, she asked him to get tested for sexually transmitted infections. She alleged Jacobs later removed her from the residence, grabbed her by the arms and biceps, pushed her against a wall and threw her belongings out.

She said she sustained bruises to her arms and swelling around her ribs. Police records indicate responding officers at the time observed "no visible signs of injury, bruising or damage consistent with a physical altercation."

The third woman: May 2022

She said she met Jacobs through social media and that he flew her to a residence. She described an altercation in which Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest and took her phone.

She said she suffered bruises and scratches but did not report it because she was not a US citizen at the time and Jacobs told her she could be deported.

Jacobs' lawyers called the allegations "uncorroborated, old, and previously unreported," noting prosecutors reviewed them before the plea deal.

The NFL said it "will review these allegations as part of the investigation, which has remained open."

headline: Pakistan warns Afghan Taliban against making its security 'hostage to inaction'
subheadline: Islamabad says it will take all necessary measures under international law to eliminate threats to national security
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan snubs Kabul's attempts to blame its policies for frayed ties.
Ministry says terror emanating from Afghan soil poisoning relations.
Islamabad says won't tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across border.

Pakistan has warned the Afghan Taliban regime that it will take all necessary measures under international law to protect its national security, saying Kabul's failure to prevent terrorist activity from Afghan soil remains the main obstacle to improving bilateral relations.

In a statement issued on Saturday, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said the Taliban leadership was continuing to blame Islamabad's policies while avoiding the central issue behind deteriorating ties: the presence of terrorist sanctuaries in Afghanistan.

"Pakistan’s position is unequivocal: terrorism is a red line, and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable," the ministry said, adding that Islamabad would not tolerate militant sanctuaries across the border that threaten its security.

The ministry said Pakistan reserved the right to take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to eliminate threats to its national security, wherever they originated.

"Pakistan’s resolve to protect its people must never be mistaken for weakness," it said, holding the Afghan Taliban regime responsible for addressing threats emanating from its territory.

The ministry further rejected what it described as attempts by Kabul to shift blame, make hollow assurances and question Pakistan's policies, saying such statements would neither resolve the crisis nor absolve the Afghan Taliban of its responsibilities.

"Pakistan’s security will not be held hostage to Afghan Taliban’s inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities," it said, urging the Taliban leadership to recognise that responsibility for preventing threats from Afghan territory rested with it.

Tensions over cross-border terrorism

headline: Spirit Halloween shooting: One dead, six injured at Fairfield store
subheadline: Fairfield police appeal for information as investigation continues
author: Web Desk
article_text:
There was a death and injuries to six people who were shot inside a Spirit Halloween shop located in Solano Town Centre in Fairfield, California, on Friday night, according to police reports.

The Fairfield Police Department was called to the store around 8:30 pm. Seven people were shot, and one person was pronounced dead at the scene. There were three people in critical condition. Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall gave this information about the condition of the wounded people.

No one is under arrest. Neither has there been any suspect named nor has the motive of the shooting been given by the police. In an early Saturday morning update, it came out that the shooting was a targeted attack by a single shooter in the store.

Detectives are actively investigating this case, going through videos and other evidence in order to identify the individual responsible for this terrible crime of violence.

Eyewitnesses reported scenes of chaos. At the time that gunfire erupted, Javier Espinoza and his girlfriend, Alicia Reyes, had completed their Halloween shopping.

The couple, along with roughly a dozen other shoppers, took cover near a security fence located at the rear end of the shopping centre, but then managed to lift the barrier and flee out of the mall.

“We’ve learned from the workplace videos about mass shootings,” Espinoza said. “Always run when you can run.” According to Meina Davis, a shoe store employee, she heard a second volley of gunfire along with the cries of a mother looking for her child. “I’m still in shock,” she said. “It’s just so surreal.”

According to the FBI Sacramento, it would send its Evidence Response Team to help. The Suisun City police and California Highway Patrol were responding too. In addition, Solano Town Centre cancelled its Halloween trick-or-treat festivities, although the mall itself stayed open on Saturday.

Rep. John Garamendi, representing the area of Fairfield, stated: “What was meant to be a day of celebration has now turned into a tragedy.”

headline: King Charles faces end of tradition last upheld by Queen Elizabeth II
subheadline: King Charles makes sad admission about beloved pastime during tour
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles has made a revealing comment about a passion that has long been part of his life.

The 77-year-old made the remark while meeting representatives of Guyana's nine Indigenous groups on Friday, during the latest leg of his nine-day autumn tour.

Charles was presented with a collection of traditional items, including Indigenous maracas used in spiritual practices, a bow and arrow, a riding crop and a whistle that mimicked the sound of an owl.

Read More: King Charles presented with unique gift after leaving conservationists impressed

The King even joked about needing the maracas for his Junkanoo parade in the Bahamas, where his Caribbean tour began.

But it was the riding crop that prompted a more reflective response. After receiving the gift, Charles remarked wistfully: "Ahh, if I go riding again on a horse."

His comment appeared to suggest that getting back in the saddle is no longer a regular part of his life, despite his long-standing love of horses.

Charles was once an accomplished polo player and jockey, with horse riding forming an important part of his life for decades.

In recent years, he stepped away from the saddle amid his ongoing cancer treatment.

According to reports in The Times, the King may have given up riding for good and is not expected to return to horseback for the annual Trooping the Colour parade.

His last appearance on horseback at the event came in 2023, marking the first time a reigning monarch had ridden in the parade since Queen Elizabeth II did so in 1986.

Charles rode Noble, a black mare presented to him by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

But the occasion did not go entirely smoothly, as the horse broke into a canter and appeared unsettled during the ceremony.

Unlike his siblings Princess Anne and Prince Edward, who have continued to enjoy riding, Charles has reportedly not been on horseback for several years.

In recent years, he stepped away from the saddle amid his ongoing cancer treatment.

According to reports in The Times, the King may have given up riding for good and is not expected to return to horseback for the annual Trooping the Colour parade.

His last appearance on horseback at the event came in 2023, marking the first time a reigning monarch had ridden in the parade since Queen Elizabeth II did so in 1986.

Charles rode Noble, a black mare presented to him by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. 

But the occasion did not go entirely smoothly, as the horse broke into a canter and appeared unsettled during the ceremony.

Unlike his siblings Princess Anne and Prince Edward, who have continued to enjoy riding, Charles has reportedly not been on horseback for several years.

headline: Candice Swanepoel spotted with gold ring as Tom Brady romance heats up
subheadline: Source revealed the two have been dating for some time
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Candice Swanepoel raised new questions about her reported romance with Tom Brady after she was spotted wearing a gold ring on her left hand.

The Victoria’s Secret model was seen out in Florida this week, and the ring quickly caught attention as dating rumours about the pair continue to grow.

Swanepoel was walking around Surfside, near Miami Beach, when she was spotted wearing the thick gold band.

She kept her look simple with black trousers, a matching top and sunglasses. However, it was the ring on her engagement finger that became the main talking point.

READ MORE: Tom Brady sparks feud between Victoria's Secret models

The sighting comes just as reports about her relationship with Brady are making headlines.

A source told People that the two have been dating for some time and have been spending a lot of time together in Miami.

But there is also another name being linked to the story. Fellow Victoria’s Secret model Joan Smalls is reportedly unhappy about their romance.

Reports claim Smalls was seeing Brady on and off between 2023 and 2024.

Swanepoel's representative has spoken about the rumours, saying that she values her long friendship with Smalls and prefers to keep her personal life private.

Neither Swanepoel nor Brady has confirmed their reported relationship.

headline: Margaret Qualley makes first appearance after Jack Antonoff divorce filing
subheadline: Margaret Qualley spotted out and about after divorce news became public
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Margaret Qualley seems to be all booked and busy professionally while her divorce with Jack Antonoff is in process.

The 32-year-old actress and the Bleachers frontman filed for the divorce after three years to their marriage, and a few months after separation.

A day after the news became public, The Substance star was spotted with Tom Holland in London where the two are seemingly preparing for their Fred Astaire biopic.

The movie stars Qualley as Adele Astaire and the Spiderman actor as Fred Astaire. Sabrina Carpenter and Talia Ryder will also appear in the movie alongside them.

READ MORE: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff file for divorce

Flocking to the comments, fans wrote, "oh we’re really in the fred astaire biopic era now," and "They're already rehearsing for the scenes."

A third chimed in, "I'm so looking forward to this biopic."

While one called out to Carpenter, writing, "@SabrinaAnnLynn leave your house please imy."

More cheered, "IM UP," and "so exciting!!!"

headline: Sydney Sweeney gets close to Michele Morrone while filming 'The Housemaid 2'
subheadline: The film became a huge success after earning more than $400 million worldwide
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Sydney Sweeney and Michele Morrone are back together on the set of The Housemaid sequel.

The two actors shared a warm moment while filming in New York City, leaving fans gushing.

Sweeney was seen hugging her co star on Friday as they got back to work on the new movie.

The actress, who plays Millie in the film, looked relaxed in green cargo pants, a denim jacket and black boots.

Morrone, who plays Enzo, the mysterious man working at the house, wore a black sweater and dark trousers.

READ MORE: Sydney Sweeney changing religion for Scooter Braun?

Their reunion comes as filming for the sequel continues. Sweeney has also been busy shooting scenes with another co star, Stephen Kalyn.

Earlier this week, the two were spotted filming a kissing scene. He plays Brock, Millie's boyfriend in the new movie.

The first film was about Millie as she started working for a wealthy family, hoping to leave her troubled past behind.

Her new job, however, soon turned into something much more dangerous than she expected.

The movie became a huge success after earning more than $400 million worldwide against a budget of just $35 million.

Sweeney has already said that she would love to play Millie again.

So now, she is getting the chance to return to the story as the sequel moves ahead.

headline: Meghan Markle unveils unexpected treat after royal family news
subheadline: Meghan Markle gives her best-selling Raspberry Spread an adorable makeover
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle has found another way to bring a little festive cheer to As Ever.

The Duchess of Sussex has introduced a limited-edition plush squeaker toy inspired by one of the brand’s best-known products, its Raspberry Spread.

Announcing the launch on Instagram, the brand shared: "A little something for your best friend, too.

Read More: Meghan Markle's UK dream turns into total humiliation with fresh blow

Inspired by our best-selling Raspberry Spread, our new limited-edition Plush Squeaker Toy brings a playful touch to the season of gifting."

The new addition follows the brand’s recent holiday candle launch, giving Meghan another product to offer customers during the festive shopping season.

The latest launch comes at a difficult moment for the Duchess, who found herself back in the headlines over reports concerning her estranged father, Thomas Markle.

Philippine authorities are reportedly investigating allegations involving the possession of child sexual abuse material, with electronic devices seized from his residence for examination.

headline: Patrick Stewart's 'Star Trek' return almost happened before his death
subheadline: His planned return will now remain a story
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Patrick Stewart had one more Star Trek story he wanted to be part of before his death.

The actor was interested in returning as Captain Jean Luc Picard in a new series, but the project never moved forward.

So now, new details have revealed just how much he wanted to be part of it.

The planned show was called Star Trek: Legacy and was meant to continue the story after Star Trek: Picard ended in 2023.

It would have brought back some familiar characters while also giving new faces a chance to join the crew.

Terry Matalas, who worked on the final season of Picard, recently spoke about the idea.

He, however, revealed that Patrick was excited about returning and even wanted to appear in the show to give missions to the new Starfleet officers.

READ MORE: Patrick Stewart's son addresses actor's death amid estrangement reports

The series was also expected to feature Jeri Ryan as Seven of Nine, along with other familiar faces.

The plan, moreover, never got approval, leaving the project unfinished.

Patrick became a much loved part of Star Trek after first playing Picard in 1987.

He continued the role for many years, making it one of the most important parts of his career.

His planned return will now remain a story that fans never got to see.

headline: US acknowledges Pakistan's concerns over cross-border terrorism from Afghanistan
subheadline: Rubio says Pakistan has taken action in response, adding that Washington does not want it targeted by terrorism
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Rubio says Pakistan concerned about terrorist attacks from Afghan territory
Says Islamabad believes Afghan Taliban failed to prevent terrorism.
Islamabad says Kabul's inaction remains main obstacle to better ties.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has acknowledged Pakistan’s concerns over terrorist attacks originating from Afghan territory, saying Washington does not want Pakistan to become a target of terrorism.

Speaking in Atlanta on Saturday at the conclusion of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting, Rubio said Pakistan was concerned about attacks being carried out from Afghanistan and believed the Afghan Taliban had failed to take sufficient action to prevent them.

"Pakistan is concerned about terrorist attacks that are being sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan. They feel that the Taliban is not doing enough to constrain those attacks, and they've taken action against it," Rubio said.

"We obviously have heard those concerns on their part. We obviously don't want them to be targeted by terrorism," he added.

Rubio’s remarks came as Islamabad renewed its criticism of the Afghan Taliban regime over what it described as Kabul’s failure to address terrorist activity originating from Afghan soil.

In a statement on Saturday, Pakistan’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting rejected remarks by Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, accusing the leadership of shifting blame to Islamabad while ignoring what it called the central issue undermining bilateral relations: terrorism emanating from Afghanistan.

The ministry said Pakistan would not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across the border and reserved the right to take all necessary measures under international law to eliminate threats to its national security.

It described the Taliban regime’s continued refusal to address terrorism as the principal obstacle to normal relations, saying Pakistan’s security would not be held hostage to the regime’s "inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities".

Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to take verifiable action against militant groups, particularly the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, which Pakistani officials accuse of operating from Afghan territory. The Taliban authorities have denied allowing militants to use Afghanistan as a base for attacks against Pakistan.

headline: Guyana's First Lady shares happy moments with King Charles after final goodbye
subheadline: King Charles takes keen interest in efforts to protect coastline
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles received a warm thank you from Guyana’s First Lady Arya Ali following his visit to one of the country’s most important coastal spaces.

The First Lady shared photographs with the monarch on social media, offering a throwback from his visit to the Kingston Seawall Esplanade.

King Charles explored the work being done to protect Guyana’s coastline and promote sustainable development.

Read More: King Charles finds shady spot before hearing First Lady's plans

In her caption, Arya described it as an honour to welcome His Majesty to the site, which she noted was among the significant family-friendly spaces revitalised through the National Beautification Project.

The tour also gave the King an opportunity to explore the Commonwealth Sustainable Cities Initiative exhibition, which featured innovative ideas for more sustainable urban development.

Environmental conservation was another key focus of the engagement, with discussions turning to mangrove restoration and management.

The monarch was joined by Guyana’s Minister of Agriculture, Zulfikar Mustapha, and Mangroves Restoration and Management Project Coordinator Kene Moseley.

In photographs from the engagement, Charles could be seen using binoculars as he learned more about the country's mangrove restoration efforts.

Mustapha explained how the mangroves serve as a natural defence against the Atlantic Ocean, helping to limit coastal erosion and flooding while protecting agricultural land.

He also spoke about their importance to local fisheries and the livelihoods of communities that depend on coastal resources.

headline: Tehran steps up military readiness as Qatar talks seek to avert renewed US strikes
subheadline: US Secretary of State Rubio says Trump has yet to decide on fresh strikes but prefers a diplomatic solution
author: Reuters
article_text:
Qatari mediators proposed seven-day US-Iran trust-building plan.
Doha coordinated frequently with US during this week's diplomacy.
Security chief says Iran debating whether to lift ban on nuclear weapons.

Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source who was briefed on the negotiations told Reuters, as diplomats try to avert new fighting after the US midterm elections this week.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Trump has held off on strikes on Iran in recent weeks ahead of midterm elections that will determine whether his Republican Party will retain its thin majorities in both houses of the US Congress.

Saturday's talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were being coordinated in regular contact with Washington.

Countries in the region have been anticipating that Trump could restart attacks once the voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

Iran's influential security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran was debating whether to lift its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons should hostilities resume, although he said no such decision had been taken. Rubio, hosting foreign ministers of the G20 major economies in Atlanta, declined to set a timeframe for the talks in Qatar, but said direct and indirect contacts with Iran were under way.

Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election to keep his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can "finish the job".

• Qatari mediators proposed seven-day US-Iran trust-building plan.
  • Doha coordinated frequently with US during this week's diplomacy.
  • Security chief says Iran debating whether to lift ban on nuclear weapons.

Iranian negotiators held talks in Doha with Qatari mediators on Saturday to discuss paths out of war in the Gulf, a source who was briefed on the negotiations told Reuters, as diplomats try to avert new fighting after the US midterm elections this week.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that President Donald Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran, but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Trump has held off on strikes on Iran in recent weeks ahead of midterm elections that will determine whether his Republican Party will retain its thin majorities in both houses of the US Congress.

Saturday's talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, said the source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The source said the talks were being coordinated in regular contact with Washington.

Countries in the region have been anticipating that Trump could restart attacks once the voting is over. Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking at US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei stated on Saturday, ordering the armed forces to be prepared to respond to any attacks. The Iranian military later announced it was taking steps to improve its readiness.

"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response," Khamenei said on Saturday in the statement posted on his official Telegram account. He has not appeared in public since replacing his father, who was slain at the war's outset.

Khamenei said senior commanders had reported high readiness along the Gulf coast, in and around the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman, and on Iran's northwestern and southeastern borders.

Iran's influential security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran was debating whether to lift its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons should hostilities resume, although he said no such decision had been taken. There could be no talks on Iran's nuclear programme unless Washington accepted Iran's demands, he added.

Rubio, hosting foreign ministers of the G20 major economies in Atlanta, declined to set a timeframe for the talks in Qatar, but said direct and indirect contacts with Iran were under way.

"There are multiple talks. Talks have actually never stopped," he said.

Trump would "prefer to solve it diplomatically. But I think what the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it," Rubio said.

Diplomacy continues despite gaps

Trump, who launched the war alongside Israel in February, has repeatedly hinted at plans to restart strikes on Iran. Last week he called on Israelis ahead of their own election to keep his wartime ally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in power so the two leaders can "finish the job".

But Washington has also lately taken steps to indicate it is open to diplomacy. Earlier this week, Vice President JD Vance, who led the US delegation at previous rounds of talks with Iran, wrote a letter to the security chief Rezaei, which the New York Times and Wall Street Journal described as an initiative to see if it was possible to restart talks.

Trump has played the letter down, saying he approved it only to discuss the possibility of letting more medical supplies into Iran: "I said if you want to do that, that's ok. Basically, it's getting supplies in ​to help people that are not well."

In the latest Qatari-mediated discussions, the Qataris brought a proposal to Tehran a week ago for a seven-day plan, under which the US and Iran would take daily steps to build trust ahead of broader peace talks, the source briefed on the negotiations said. A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday that this proposal was not deemed satisfactory by Tehran.

Iran has been proposing its own seven-day plan since September, so far rejected by Trump. That calls for Washington to lift a blockade of Iranian ports, unfreeze assets and approve an Iranian-backed route through the Strait of Hormuz, after which the contested strait would be reopened.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in remarks reported by Al Jazeera on Saturday that Iran was studying Vance's letter. He said the Iranian plan was the only proposal on the table to reopen the strait.

headline: Claudia Sulewski and Finneas are still on cloud nine two months after wedding
subheadline: They married on August 29 in California
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Claudia Sulewski and Finneas O’Connell are still enjoying the happiness of their wedding.

Now it seems like the special day is something they cannot stop thinking about.

Even after two months of marriage, the couple is still holding on to those beautiful memories.

The actress and skincare brand founder recently spoke about her married life while attending the 2026 WWD Honors in New York City.

She shared that life with Finneas has been wonderful, but they still miss the excitement of their wedding day.

READ MORE: Finneas officially shares first set of wedding photos with new wife Claudia

“Oh, we’re blissed out,” Sulewski said. “We’re still experiencing the withdrawals of that being the best day of our lives and it now being behind us. But it’s so good.

We’re so happy, and just truly, best day of our lives.”

The star, however, also shared that getting married brought her feelings she never experienced before.

For her, it was not just another happy moment, but something completely new.

“New feeling unlocked, that’s what I keep saying. The feelings we felt on that day, I have never felt ever in my life before,” she added.

The couple first met on a dating app in 2018 and got engaged in 2025.

They married on August 29 in California, with Finneas' sister, Billie Eilish, leading the ceremony.

Now, the newlyweds are also getting ready for Halloween. Sulewski revealed that they are planning matching costumes this year.

headline: Is a bureaucratic mindset the missing link?
subheadline: Persistence and apparent worsening of governance problems warrant critical examination of underlying causes
author: Javaid Jehangir
article_text:
The ongoing debate on governance challenges and reforms in Pakistan raises a fundamental question: why have successive governments, despite repeated reform initiatives and substantial investments of time, money, expertise and institutional resources, failed to achieve commensurate improvements in governance?

The persistence, and in several areas the apparent worsening, of governance problems demands a critical examination of the underlying causes. Are these failures primarily attributable to flawed reform design and weak implementation, or have we overlooked a deeper institutional problem: the bureaucratic mindset, organisational culture and administrative practices through which reforms are conceived, interpreted and implemented?

Successive reform initiatives may have suffered from inadequate planning, unrealistic objectives or weak implementation mechanisms. Yet another possibility deserves equal attention: governments have focused too much on changing rules, procedures, organisational structures and administrative arrangements without adequately addressing the institutional culture that shapes how these changes translate into practice. Revising regulations or restructuring departments is relatively straightforward; transforming entrenched attitudes, behavioural patterns, incentives and power relationships is considerably more difficult. Without such transformation, even well-designed reforms risk producing formal changes without meaningful improvements in governance.

Pakistan inherited an administrative system designed primarily to maintain law and order, exercise control and protect the interests of the colonial state. Centralised decision-making, rigid hierarchies, extensive discretionary authority and a considerable distance between officials and citizens were integral to that model. Although independence changed the state’s political status, many features of its colonial administrative culture survived.

Subsequent political and institutional developments reinforced rather than fundamentally transformed these practices. Official authority increasingly became associated with status, privilege, and access to power, while administrative procedures often took precedence over the public purposes they were meant to serve. Citizens seeking routine services or redress frequently encounter cumbersome processes, avoidable delays and officials more concerned with procedural objections than with resolving legitimate problems.

A related institutional weakness is the dominance of the generalist model in Pakistan’s civil service. The system has traditionally assumed that broad administrative experience equips officers for leadership across diverse fields, often giving generalists an advantage over professionals with specialised knowledge. Administrative coordination and broad policy understanding are undoubtedly important, but they cannot substitute for technical competence in increasingly complex areas of governance.

Public financial management, taxation, energy, economic planning, engineering, climate change and digital transformation require substantial professional expertise. Effective governance demands a combination of administrative judgement, technical knowledge and the ability to coordinate across disciplines. A system that undervalues specialised competence risks weakening the quality of policy formulation and implementation.

The generalist model is compounded by an informal hierarchy among civil service occupational groups. The 1973 administrative reforms established different services to perform distinct governmental functions. However, certain groups, particularly the Pakistan Administrative Service and the Police Service of Pakistan, have traditionally enjoyed greater prestige, visibility and access to influential policymaking and leadership positions.

The issue is not the importance of field administration or law enforcement, both of which are essential state functions. It is the institutional imbalance that arises when occupational affiliation, rather than relevant expertise, demonstrated performance and professional merit, disproportionately determines career progression and access to senior positions. Such hierarchies can discourage specialists, weaken professional recognition and prevent the state from fully utilising the expertise available within its own institutions.

These structural features are reinforced by a bureaucratic culture in which procedural and regulatory compliance frequently takes precedence over public outcomes. Rules and procedures are indispensable for legality, consistency and accountability, but they become counterproductive when treated as ends in themselves rather than instruments for serving the public interest.

Excessive procedural tilt can delay decisions, discourage initiative, blur responsibility for results and make public institutions less responsive to citizens. Processing files, observing formalities and avoiding procedural objections cannot, by themselves, demonstrate effective administration. Institutional performance must also be judged by the fairness of decisions, the quality and timeliness of services, the efficient use of public resources and the ability to resolve public problems. The objective should not be to weaken rules, but to ensure they are applied fairly and proportionately to achieve their intended purposes.

The relationship between political leadership and the civil service presents another fundamental challenge. Elected governments are entitled to set public policy, while civil servants must implement lawful decisions impartially and professionally. Problems arise when political patronage, arbitrary transfers, insecure tenures and promotions divorced from merit displace established administrative standards. These practices undermine continuity, weaken institutional memory and discourage officers from offering candid advice or resisting improper directions. They also create incentives for officials to prioritize the preferences of influential decision-makers over institutional responsibilities and public interest.

A professional bureaucracy must therefore be responsive to elected governments without becoming an instrument of partisan interests. Transparent posting and transfer policies, reasonable tenure protection, merit-based promotions and credible disciplinary mechanisms are essential to this objective. However, administrative independence must not become a shield against accountability. Civil servants must answer for their decisions, conduct and results, with meaningful consequences for misconduct, abuse of authority and persistent incompetence. The objective is a politically impartial but professionally accountable civil service in which elected leaders respect administrative standards and officials exercise their lawful authority in the public interest.

Addressing these weaknesses requires a more integrated and professionally balanced civil service. Recruitment, career progression and appointments to leadership positions should reflect merit, integrity, relevant expertise and demonstrated performance rather than occupational affiliation or proximity to influential decision-makers. Generalists and specialists should complement one another, with responsibilities and authority aligned with institutional needs and professional competence. This requires reviewing barriers that prevent specialists from taking leadership roles for which they have the relevant qualifications and experience. The purpose is not to replace one privileged group with another, but to dismantle unjustified hierarchies and strengthen the collective capacity of the state.

Transforming institutional culture must begin with recruitment, training and professional development. Training academies do more than impart technical knowledge; they shape professional identity, attitudes towards authority and perceptions of citizens. If training reinforces an exaggerated sense of official status or a narrow emphasis on procedural compliance, it can perpetuate the very attitudes that reform seeks to change. Professional preparation should therefore cultivate integrity, independent thinking, empathy, respect for the rule of law and a commitment to public service. It should also strengthen problem-solving, evidence-based decision-making and the capacity to work across professional disciplines.

Digital technologies and artificial intelligence can support this transformation by simplifying procedures, improving access to information, reducing avoidable delays and strengthening transparency. However, technology cannot compensate for institutional resistance, weak accountability or an unwillingness to change established practices. Digitising an unnecessarily complicated procedure may simply reproduce inefficiency in electronic form. Technology must therefore be accompanied by process simplification, appropriate safeguards, professional judgement and clear responsibility for decisions. A citizen-centred administration does not dispense with rules or due process; it applies them consistently and proportionately while remaining focused on legitimate public needs.

Ultimately, reform must also change the incentives that shape administrative behavior. Performance assessment should extend beyond procedural compliance to include service quality, timeliness, efficiency, fairness and measurable results. Recruitment and promotion must reward competence and integrity, while transparent, predictable rules must constrain political interference in routine administrative decisions. At the same time, institutions must hold officials accountable for poor performance and misuse of authority. Without changes to these underlying incentives, new rules, organisational structures and technologies are unlikely to deliver lasting improvements.

The effectiveness of governance reforms depends not simply on what governments introduce, but on how public institutions understand, own and implement those reforms.

A bureaucratic mindset is not the only cause of Pakistan’s governance deficit, but it is a critical missing link between reform intentions and actual results. Unless institutional culture, professional incentives and administrative behaviour evolve alongside formal changes, successive reform initiatives risk reproducing the very failures they are intended to correct.

Pakistan’s challenge is therefore not merely to redesign its bureaucratic machinery, but to transform its purpose and mindset: from an institution primarily concerned with authority and procedural control into a professional, responsive, accountable and citizen-centred public service. Without that transformation, governance reform will remain more visible in official announcements than in the everyday experience of citizens.

The writer is the former auditor general of Pakistan.

The persistence, and in several areas the apparent worsening, of governance problems demands a critical examination of the underlying causes. Are these failures primarily attributable to flawed reform design and weak implementation, or have we overlooked a deeper institutional problem: the bureaucratic mindset, organisational culture and administrative practices through which reforms are conceived, interpreted and implemented?

Successive reform initiatives may have suffered from inadequate planning, unrealistic objectives or weak implementation mechanisms. Yet another possibility deserves equal attention: governments have focused too much on changing rules, procedures, organisational structures and administrative arrangements without adequately addressing the institutional culture that shapes how these changes translate into practice. Revising regulations or restructuring departments is relatively straightforward; transforming entrenched attitudes, behavioural patterns, incentives and power relationships is considerably more difficult. Without such transformation, even well-designed reforms risk producing formal changes without meaningful improvements in governance.

Pakistan inherited an administrative system designed primarily to maintain law and order, exercise control and protect the interests of the colonial state. Centralised decision-making, rigid hierarchies, extensive discretionary authority and a considerable distance between officials and citizens were integral to that model. Although independence changed the state’s political status, many features of its colonial administrative culture survived.

Subsequent political and institutional developments reinforced rather than fundamentally transformed these practices. Official authority increasingly became associated with status, privilege, and access to power, while administrative procedures often took precedence over the public purposes they were meant to serve. Citizens seeking routine services or redress frequently encounter cumbersome processes, avoidable delays and officials more concerned with procedural objections than with resolving legitimate problems.

A related institutional weakness is the dominance of the generalist model in Pakistan’s civil service. The system has traditionally assumed that broad administrative experience equips officers for leadership across diverse fields, often giving generalists an advantage over professionals with specialised knowledge. Administrative coordination and broad policy understanding are undoubtedly important, but they cannot substitute for technical competence in increasingly complex areas of governance.

Public financial management, taxation, energy, economic planning, engineering, climate change and digital transformation require substantial professional expertise. Effective governance demands a combination of administrative judgement, technical knowledge and the ability to coordinate across disciplines. A system that undervalues specialised competence risks weakening the quality of policy formulation and implementation.

The generalist model is compounded by an informal hierarchy among civil service occupational groups. The 1973 administrative reforms established different services to perform distinct governmental functions. However, certain groups, particularly the Pakistan Administrative Service and the Police Service of Pakistan, have traditionally enjoyed greater prestige, visibility and access to influential policymaking and leadership positions.

The issue is not the importance of field administration or law enforcement, both of which are essential state functions. It is the institutional imbalance that arises when occupational affiliation, rather than relevant expertise, demonstrated performance and professional merit, disproportionately determines career progression and access to senior positions. Such hierarchies can discourage specialists, weaken professional recognition and prevent the state from fully utilising the expertise available within its own institutions.

These structural features are reinforced by a bureaucratic culture in which procedural and regulatory compliance frequently takes precedence over public outcomes. Rules and procedures are indispensable for legality, consistency and accountability, but they become counterproductive when treated as ends in themselves rather than instruments for serving the public interest.

Excessive procedural tilt can delay decisions, discourage initiative, blur responsibility for results and make public institutions less responsive to citizens. Processing files, observing formalities and avoiding procedural objections cannot, by themselves, demonstrate effective administration. Institutional performance must also be judged by the fairness of decisions, the quality and timeliness of services, the efficient use of public resources and the ability to resolve public problems. The objective should not be to weaken rules, but to ensure they are applied fairly and proportionately to achieve their intended purposes.

The relationship between political leadership and the civil service presents another fundamental challenge. Elected governments are entitled to set public policy, while civil servants must implement lawful decisions impartially and professionally. Problems arise when political patronage, arbitrary transfers, insecure tenures and promotions divorced from merit displace established administrative standards. These practices undermine continuity, weaken institutional memory and discourage officers from offering candid advice or resisting improper directions. They also create incentives for officials to prioritize the preferences of influential decision-makers over institutional responsibilities and public interest.

A professional bureaucracy must therefore be responsive to elected governments without becoming an instrument of partisan interests. Transparent posting and transfer policies, reasonable tenure protection, merit-based promotions and credible disciplinary mechanisms are essential to this objective. However, administrative independence must not become a shield against accountability. Civil servants must answer for their decisions, conduct and results, with meaningful consequences for misconduct, abuse of authority and persistent incompetence. The objective is a politically impartial but professionally accountable civil service in which elected leaders respect administrative standards and officials exercise their lawful authority in the public interest.

Addressing these weaknesses requires a more integrated and professionally balanced civil service. Recruitment, career progression and appointments to leadership positions should reflect merit, integrity, relevant expertise and demonstrated performance rather than occupational affiliation or proximity to influential decision-makers. Generalists and specialists should complement one another, with responsibilities and authority aligned with institutional needs and professional competence. This requires reviewing barriers that prevent specialists from taking leadership roles for which they have the relevant qualifications and experience. The purpose is not to replace one privileged group with another, but to dismantle unjustified hierarchies and strengthen the collective capacity of the state.

Transforming institutional culture must begin with recruitment, training and professional development. Training academies do more than impart technical knowledge; they shape professional identity, attitudes towards authority and perceptions of citizens. If training reinforces an exaggerated sense of official status or a narrow emphasis on procedural compliance, it can perpetuate the very attitudes that reform seeks to change. Professional preparation should therefore cultivate integrity, independent thinking, empathy, respect for the rule of law and a commitment to public service. It should also strengthen problem-solving, evidence-based decision-making and the capacity to work across professional disciplines.

Digital technologies and artificial intelligence can support this transformation by simplifying procedures, improving access to information, reducing avoidable delays and strengthening transparency. However, technology cannot compensate for institutional resistance, weak accountability or an unwillingness to change established practices. Digitising an unnecessarily complicated procedure may simply reproduce inefficiency in electronic form. Technology must therefore be accompanied by process simplification, appropriate safeguards, professional judgement and clear responsibility for decisions. A citizen-centred administration does not dispense with rules or due process; it applies them consistently and proportionately while remaining focused on legitimate public needs.

Ultimately, reform must also change the incentives that shape administrative behavior. Performance assessment should extend beyond procedural compliance to include service quality, timeliness, efficiency, fairness and measurable results. Recruitment and promotion must reward competence and integrity, while transparent, predictable rules must constrain political interference in routine administrative decisions. At the same time, institutions must hold officials accountable for poor performance and misuse of authority. Without changes to these underlying incentives, new rules, organisational structures and technologies are unlikely to deliver lasting improvements.

The effectiveness of governance reforms depends not simply on what governments introduce, but on how public institutions understand, own and implement those reforms.

A bureaucratic mindset is not the only cause of Pakistan’s governance deficit, but it is a critical missing link between reform intentions and actual results. Unless institutional culture, professional incentives and administrative behaviour evolve alongside formal changes, successive reform initiatives risk reproducing the very failures they are intended to correct.

Pakistan’s challenge is therefore not merely to redesign its bureaucratic machinery, but to transform its purpose and mindset: from an institution primarily concerned with authority and procedural control into a professional, responsive, accountable and citizen-centred public service. Without that transformation, governance reform will remain more visible in official announcements than in the everyday experience of citizens.

The writer is the former auditor general of Pakistan.

headline: Fakhar Zaman levels Saeed Anwar's record with ton in tri-series final
subheadline: Left-handed opening batter scores 127 runs off 99 deliveries, studded with 11 fours and six sixes in final
author: Sports Desk
article_text:
Pakistan's left-handed opener Fakhar Zaman on Saturday equalled the long-standing record set by batting great Saeed Anwar, scoring a century against Sri Lanka in the final of the home ODI tri-series at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium.

Fakhar, who opened the innings for Pakistan after the home side were set a daunting 326-run target in the summit clash by Sri Lanka, proved his credentials of performing in big matches by bringing up his 12th century in the format off just 84 deliveries.

He eventually went on to score 127 runs off 99 deliveries, studded with 11 fours and six sixes, before falling victim to Dilshan Madushanka in the 34th over of the innings.

The brisk century was Fakhar's second in an ODI tournament final, with the first being his ton against traditional rivals India in the summit clash of the ICC Men's Champions Trophy 2017 at The Oval in London.

Consequently, Fakhar equalled legendary batter Anwar's record of scoring the most, two centuries, in an ODI tournament final by a Pakistani batter.

The former Pakistan opener had set the benchmark by scoring hundreds against Sri Lanka in the 1993 Wills Trophy final and against fierce rivals at the Silver Jubilee Independence Cup in 1998.

Furthermore, the 127-run knock also bolstered Fakhar's ODI runs tally past the 4000-run barrier, becoming only the 16th Pakistani batter to achieve the milestone, joining the likes of Inzamam-ul-Haq, Javed Miandad, Younis Khan and Anwar.

For the unversed, Fakhar has now scored 4,019 runs in 96 innings in the format at a formidable average of 44.65 and a strike rate of 93.57. Besides 12 centuries, the left-handed batter also has 19 fifties to his name in ODIs.

headline: Shocking Palace connection in Meghan's father case comes to light
subheadline: Palace gets dragged into Thomas Markle Sr case as new details uncovered amid probe
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle’s father Thomas Markle Sr is currently under investigation for allegations of holding child pornographic material and child abuse after the disturbing news surfaced last month.

The Duchess of Sussex had expressed her distress over the news, revealing that she had known about it since 2019. Hence, the reason why she has not wanted to reconcile with her father neither let her children meet him.

Even though the Palace has distanced itself via sources claiming that the matter is “for the Sussex household”.

READ MORE: What happened in Palace when Meghan learned father's allegations?

Reports also claimed that the Palace was not informed of the allegations at the time. However, the latest developments paint a very different picture.

Prince Harry’s wife had received a letter from Thomas Sr’s first wife Roslyn Loveless – who passed away in 2024 – about the claims. Meghan had wanted to go public with the matter but she was forced to stay silent by one of the Palace staffers.

One of her Royalty and Specialist Protection [RaSP] bodyguards reportedly told her: “Leave it with us, we’ll investigate it.”

Seven years later, the matter was not investigated due to the incident taking place abroad. But the information was also not passed on the relevant authorities, The Times reported.

The Met are trying to identify and find the office in question. A source from Met criticised that they failed to understand the significance of the letter.

“RaSP would only have been interested in what it meant for the security of the Duke and Duchess [of Sussex]. Having assessed that, they should have thought about the wider consequences.”

Meanwhile, sources have also claimed that Harry and Meghan’s bodyguards were aware of the allegations but their closest advisors at Kensington Palace at the time were reportedly kept in the dark.

The Duchess of Sussex had expressed her distress over the news, revealing that she had known about it since 2019. Hence, the reason why she has not wanted to reconcile with her father neither let her children meet him.

Reports also claimed that the Palace was not informed of the allegations at the time. However, the latest developments paint a very different picture.

Prince Harry’s wife had received a letter from Thomas Sr’s first wife Roslyn Loveless – who passed away in 2024 – about the claims. Meghan had wanted to go public with the matter but she was forced to stay silent by one of the Palace staffers.

One of her Royalty and Specialist Protection [RaSP] bodyguards reportedly told her: “Leave it with us, we’ll investigate it.”

Seven years later, the matter was not investigated due to the incident taking place abroad. But the information was also not passed on the relevant authorities, The Times reported.

The Met are trying to identify and find the office in question. A source from Met criticised that they failed to understand the significance of the letter.

“RaSP would only have been interested in what it meant for the security of the Duke and Duchess [of Sussex]. Having assessed that, they should have thought about the wider consequences.”

Meanwhile, sources have also claimed that Harry and Meghan’s bodyguards were aware of the allegations but their closest advisors at Kensington Palace at the time were reportedly kept in the dark.
